models.name: Kimi K3
models.capabilityDelta: WAIC Shanghai launch. MoE 2.8T total; ~16/896 experts active. Official blog: still trails Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol overall but tops many other models; independent Arena/AA ranks often top-3. API ~$0.30 cache-hit / $3 miss / $15 out per M. gaps.title: No open-weight or distill response in the K3 / GLM-5.2 / Inkling era
gaps.description: July 2026 is defined by open-weight frontier parity: Kimi K3 (~2.8T, Jul 16), GLM-5.2 (MIT, long-horizon), and Inkling (Apache 2.0 multimodal, Jul 15). Builders, startups, and cost-sensitive enterprises can self-host near-frontier models. Grok remains closed-only with no announced distill/open ladder. OpenRouter mid-2026 windows show Chinese-origin models often 30–46%+ of multi-model token volume — structural cost pressure, not a news cycle.
gaps.recommendedAction: Decide and ship a public response — full open, partial distill, or hybrid open small + closed flagship — with clear licensing and HF/API distribution within one release cycle. Silence cedes builder mindshare.

gaps.title: Public frontier generation lag vs GPT-5.6 Sol, Fable 5, and K3
gaps.description: Closed frontier jumped: Claude Fable 5 (Jun 9 / restored Jul 1) and GPT-5.6 Sol (Jul 9 GA) own the Western SOTA narrative for coding and long-horizon agents. K3 simultaneously owns open-weight narrative. Grok 4.5 is competitive on some agentic boards (e.g. Design Arena near GLM-5.2) but is not the default answer to "what's the current frontier model?" in Jul 2026 coverage.
gaps.recommendedAction: Publish transparent coding/agent benchmarks vs Sol and Fable; accelerate next flagship or Grok Build specialized SOTA claims with eval harnesses journalists can reproduce.

gaps.title: Agentic coding product incomplete vs Codex Work, Claude Code, and open SWE agents
gaps.description: Token spend and enterprise ARR growth concentrate in coding agents. OpenAI packaged Sol into ChatGPT Work + Codex; Anthropic into Claude Code/Desktop; open models (GLM-5.2, K3, Inkling) flood self-host agent harnesses. Grok Build + grok-build-0.1 exist, but managed cloud agents, IDE depth, and Cursor productization remain incomplete pre-close (Q3 2026).
gaps.recommendedAction: Ship explicit Grok Build product milestones weekly through Cursor close; managed agents + multi-repo IDE + public coding leaderboard placement.

gaps.title: Agentic harness packaging lag (long-horizon jobs as product, not chat)
gaps.description: Market prices multi-hour agency: Kimi K3 demos 24–48h coding/research loops; GLM-5.2 is "built for long-horizon"; OpenAI/Anthropic ship Work/Cowork/Code with durable artifacts and computer use. Grok model quality is competitive (e.g. strong Terminal-Bench); conversion fails when multi-hour runs, dashboards, computer use, and harness-normalized evals are not productized. Distinct from Cursor deal execution.
competitorExamples: Kimi Work + Kimi Code long-horizon demos
gaps.recommendedAction: Ship web-first Grok Work for multi-hour jobs with durable artifacts; first-class computer use; publish harness-normalized benches vs Claude Code / Codex / Kimi Code (same runner).

gaps.title: Cost ladder and release cadence vs Chinese open MoE velocity
gaps.description: DeepSeek V4 set the cost floor; GLM-5.2 claims ~1/6 US API cost on long-horizon coding; K3 demand crashed capacity within days of launch — proof of global appetite for cheap frontier-adjacent intelligence. Grok must win price/perf and throughput narratives or lose agent-builder volume permanently.
gaps.recommendedAction: Publish price/perf ladder (flagship + Build + economy), throughput SLAs, and weekly CN competitive briefings for PMs. Optional open distill if closed-only loses share.

gaps.title: Cursor / Grok Build not yet the locked enterprise coding platform
gaps.description: SpaceX $60B Cursor deal is only valuable if Grok becomes default model + managed agents + enterprise controls inside Cursor before Claude Code / Codex re-anchor budgets. Grok 4.5 is already in Cursor on all plans — attention window is open now; stalls until Q3 close or after free promo end are execution risk on a $60B asset.
gaps.recommendedAction: Public migration roadmap; interim Build feature parity checklist; day-1 post-close single-brand experience.

gaps.title: No polished desktop Work super-app
gaps.description: Claude Desktop (Chat/Cowork/Code) and ChatGPT desktop Work+Codex (Jul 9, including Free) own the knowledge-work desktop surface. Important for prosumer/enterprise sticky usage — but secondary this month to model/open shocks.
gaps.recommendedAction: Ship Grok Desktop with Chat + Work + Build tabs; differentiate with real-time search and Imagine canvas.

gaps.title: No formal funded partner / consultant network
gaps.description: OpenAI ($150M, 300k consultants target) and Anthropic ($100M CPN) are locking SI/consultant channel mindshare for enterprise deployments. Slower-burning than open-weight shock but decisive for 2026–27 enterprise pipeline.
gaps.recommendedAction: Launch funded Grok Partner Network with certification, co-sell, and public directory this half.

gaps.title: Enterprise exists but public GTM visibility lags
gaps.description: SSO/SCIM/RBAC/SOC2 exist on Grok Business. Competitors win inbound via case studies, ROI pages, and transparent sales motion. Capability is not the gap — discoverability and trust packaging is.
gaps.recommendedAction: Public enterprise pages, named case studies, compliance matrix, ROI calculator.

gaps.title: Imagine capable but under-amplified vs Sol hardware and open multimodal bases
gaps.description: Grok Imagine (image/video/agent canvas) is real capability. OpenAI amplifies Codex with Micro hardware; Inkling owns open multimodal base narrative. Packaging and ecosystem, not model absence.
gaps.recommendedAction: Creator collab / hardware; public Agent Mode showcases; API-first creative agent kits.

gaps.title: No full education / Academy stack vs Google
gaps.description: Gemini for Education + Academy + Skills Boost create long-term lock-in. Lower urgency than open-weight/coding war.
competitorExamples: Gemini for Education / Academy / Skills Boost
gaps.recommendedAction: Grok Academy paths + monthly webinars tied to partner certs.

gaps.title: Limited hackathon / community sponsorship scale
gaps.description: Grokathon exists; scale lags competitive intensity. Lowest urgency relative to Jul 2026 model shocks.
competitorExamples: OpenAI / Anthropic / Google / cloud hackathon calendars
gaps.recommendedAction: Expand Grokathon cadence with Build + Imagine + open-weight tracks if strategy allows.

roadmapItems.title: Core Grok and API leadership scorecard
roadmapItems.summary: Run one portfolio scorecard for quality, latency, cost, reliability, and real-time differentiation across consumer and API surfaces.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Give leadership a release-readiness view and defend Grok's price-performance position against fast-moving open-weight competitors.
successSignals: Weekly quality, latency, cost, and reliability review is operating
Every frontier release has a named response or no-response decision
API value proposition is consistent across product and GTM surfaces
roadmapItems.rationale: Core model and API leadership is the foundation for every suite product and needs a single Director-level operating view.

roadmapItems.title: Unify Grok Build and Cursor
roadmapItems.summary: Sequence the CLI, IDE, managed-agent, and enterprise-control surfaces into one coherent Grok Build portfolio.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Make Grok Build the default enterprise coding-agent platform with a clear migration story.
successSignals: Unified product architecture and naming decision
Published migration milestones for managed and enterprise customers
Shared enterprise controls across CLI, IDE, and cloud agents
roadmapItems.rationale: The coding portfolio is the highest-leverage near-term opportunity and the most visible integration risk.

roadmapItems.title: Enterprise proof and GTM system
roadmapItems.summary: Package existing SSO, SCIM, compliance, deployment, and support capabilities into a credible enterprise buying journey.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Convert real enterprise capability into visible trust, pipeline, and adoption.
successSignals: Public compliance and deployment matrix
Repeatable ROI narrative and sales enablement kit
Named or anonymized enterprise proof points
roadmapItems.rationale: Enterprise SSO exists; the immediate gap is packaging, proof, and buyer confidence rather than core identity functionality.

roadmapItems.title: Launch Grok Desktop Work
roadmapItems.summary: Create a unified desktop experience with Chat, Work, Build, search, and Imagine workflows on macOS and Windows.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Establish Grok as a daily knowledge-work environment rather than a collection of separate capabilities.
successSignals: Coherent desktop information architecture and prototype
Cross-surface task handoff between Work, Build, and Imagine
Clear free, paid, business, and enterprise packaging
roadmapItems.rationale: Competitors are consolidating agentic work into desktop super-apps, while Grok's differentiation is fragmented across surfaces.

roadmapItems.title: Establish the Grok Partner Network
roadmapItems.summary: Build certification, co-sell, implementation, and directory mechanics for global and boutique service partners.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Scale enterprise deployment capacity and create a trusted channel around the Grok suite.
successSignals: Partner tier and incentive design approved
Initial implementation partners recruited
Certification and co-sell pilot operating
roadmapItems.rationale: A credible services ecosystem expands reach and reduces adoption friction without requiring all deployment capacity in-house.

roadmapItems.title: Package Imagine as a creator platform
roadmapItems.summary: Turn Imagine and Agent Mode into an end-to-end creative workflow with stronger product packaging, showcases, and creator distribution.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Differentiate the Grok suite through integrated creative production rather than isolated generation features.
successSignals: Repeatable multi-step creator workflows
Creator launch program and flagship showcases
Hardware collaboration or controller decision
roadmapItems.rationale: Imagine is capable but under-packaged relative to competing creative and hardware ecosystems.

roadmapItems.title: Launch Grok Academy and certification
roadmapItems.summary: Create role-based learning paths for builders, educators, enterprise administrators, and implementation partners.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Increase adoption, partner readiness, and long-term preference through a structured learning system.
successSignals: Builder and administrator learning paths live
Certification tied to partner program
Recurring educator and enterprise webinar cadence
roadmapItems.rationale: Education compounds product adoption and supplies the enablement layer required by partners and enterprise customers.

roadmapItems.title: Scale Grokathon and community programs
roadmapItems.summary: Expand hackathons into recurring university, enterprise, Build, and Imagine tracks with meaningful sponsorship and prizes.
roadmapItems.desiredOutcome: Grow the builder pipeline and create visible proof of what the complete Grok suite enables.
successSignals: Recurring global event calendar
University and enterprise sponsorship tracks
Winning projects move into showcase or partner programs
roadmapItems.rationale: A scaled community motion turns product capability into distribution, talent, and ecosystem momentum.
